skill.name: apple-text-hyperframes
skill.description: Use when creating Apple-inspired kinetic text and UI-motion HyperFrames videos with masked typography, glossy contrast scenes, sparse copy, and synced sound cues.
whenToUse: Creating Apple-inspired HyperFrames videos with kinetic text, product-launch pacing, glossy UI motion, or premium typography
Improving a HyperFrames cut that needs masked text layers, fast-but-soft easing, motion blur, and contrasty stage lighting
Combining sparse launch copy with text, UI panels, glass surfaces, light sweeps, and sound cues that land on motion beats
Adapting the Apple-style cues reference without copying a source video shot exactly

keyConcepts.explanation: Prefer short 9:16 HyperFrames cuts around 10-18 seconds, with one product or concept name, one short verb phrase, and a few supporting labels.
Treat text as physical layers in space. Put lines inside overflow-hidden masks, animate the inner text, and use separate duplicate layers for highlights or shadows.
Use fast intent and soft landing: 0.35-0.7 second reveals, power3.out or expo.out easing, 0.04-0.12 second staggers, and a small background or UI response on every text hit.
Use restrained high-contrast stages: near-black with rim light, bright white with dark type, or a saturated product-color field with white type and dark glass overlays.
Use minimal synthetic UI sounds such as whooshes, ticks, sub hits, airy reverses, and soft chimes. Place transients on the exact frame where text settles or the mask completes.
After editing, run checks, render, and inspect representative frames for blank scenes, clipped text, low contrast, crowded copy, and audio beats that feel detached from motion.

apiReference.signature: Read references/apple-style-cues.md when Apple-style detail is requested
apiReference.purpose: Load the reference only when the user asks for Apple-style text animation, the NaughtyyJuan reference, source-video cues, or sound-layer guidance.
Standard DOM structure for masked text reveals in HyperFrames compositions.
Animate text from below an overflow-hidden mask while opacity and blur resolve into a sharp landing.
Register the main GSAP timeline so HyperFrames can render deterministic animation and audio timing.
apiReference.example:
window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
window.__timelines["main"] = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });

apiReference.purpose: Store local sound-design assets with the project topic and follow the project's existing audio convention when present.

apiReference.signature: npm run check && npm run render
apiReference.purpose: Validate and render the HyperFrames project, then inspect representative frames and audio/video sync before returning the final MP4.

gotchas: Preserve the active index.html into variants/ before replacing a HyperFrames composition.
Do not use copyrighted Apple sounds unless the user provides licensed audio; generate or source clean synthetic UI sounds instead.
Keep copy sparse. Apple-style motion falls apart when the frame is crowded with captions or long sentences.
Keep letter spacing at 0 and use weight, size, contrast, masking, and timing for polish.
Background motion should be quieter than text motion, with one primary motion direction per beat.
Avoid low-contrast gray-on-gray type unless the text is very large and still clearly readable.
Sync sound to impact frames, not scene starts; whooshes usually begin 4-8 frames before visual landing.
Patch and rerender if preview frames show clipped text, blank frames, low contrast, or text that feels disconnected from audio beats.
